stories.headline: US, Iran make contradicting claims on peace deal, clash on nuclear issue
stories.summary: Iran has denied agreeing to give up its enriched uranium as part of a US ceasefire deal, contradicting US claims. A senior Iranian source stated that the nuclear issue was not part of the preliminary agreement and that Tehran has not accepted any action on the matter. This comes after weeks of talks between the US and Iran aimed at reaching a long-term peace deal, which have been hindered by disagreements on key issues. An Iranian foreign ministry spokesman noted that while positions had been converging, agreements on key issues were not guaranteed. The US has been pushing for Iran to temper its nuclear ambitions, but Iranian officials have deemed these demands "unreasonable" and "excessive". The conflicting claims highlight the ongoing impasse between the two nations.

stories.headline: A $2.89 trillion military surge signals the sharpest global arms buildup since WWII
stories.summary: Global military spending reached a record $2.89 trillion in 2025, marking the 11th consecutive annual increase. This surge is among the sharpest increases since World War II, with a 9.4% rise from the previous year. European nations led the surge, driven by NATO members' accelerated defense investments tied to the war in Ukraine, with a 14% increase in defense spending. In contrast, US military expenditure declined by 7.5% in 2025. Countries such as Germany, Poland, and the Nordic and Baltic states made significant percentage increases in their defense spending. The trend may continue, potentially pushing annual global defense expenditure over $3 trillion by next year, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. This extraordinary scale of spending reflects a significant shift in global military priorities.

stories.headline: ‘Nightmare for Israel’: Senior GOP senators criticize alleged terms of emerging Iran deal
stories.summary: Senior Republican US senators are criticizing the reported terms of the deal US President Donald Trump is negotiating with Tehran to end the Iran war. Senators, including Tom Cotton and Lindsey Graham, warn that the emerging agreement could leave Tehran strengthened in the region. Iranian officials stated that nuclear issues are not part of the current talks, fueling concerns among Republican lawmakers. The criticism comes as US and Iranian officials signal progress toward a memorandum of understanding to end the war. Senator Graham described a deal that preserves Iran's power as a "nightmare for Israel," highlighting concerns about the agreement's potential impact on regional stability and Israel's security. The senators' warnings suggest that the deal may face opposition from Republican lawmakers if it is perceived as benefiting Iran at the expense of US allies in the region.

stories.headline: Anthropic’s founder warns AI could self-improve by 2028 and admits underestimating the risks
stories.summary: Jack Clark, co-founder and head of policy at Anthropic, warns that artificial intelligence could achieve "recursive self-improvement" by 2028, allowing AI models to autonomously enhance themselves. He estimates a better-than-even chance, around 60%, that an AI model will be able to fully train its successor by the end of 2028. Clark acknowledges that the rapid pace of AI evolution has been underestimated, even by Anthropic, leaving the company unprepared for the risks posed by advanced AI. The prediction is based on benchmark gains and longer runtimes, with Clark noting that the speed of technological advancements is likely to accelerate further. Anthropic has released a formal research agenda, prioritizing AI-driven R&D, including the development of systems that can improve their own development. Clark's warning highlights the need for preparedness and safety measures as AI capabilities continue to advance.

stories.headline: New Wear OS 7 from Google: All You Need To Know Wear OS 7 brings 10% better battery life, Gemini, and Live Updates in 2026. Let's see what's actually changing on your wrist.
stories.summary: Wear OS 7, the latest update to Google's wearable operating system, is set to bring several improvements, including a 10% increase in battery life. The update will also introduce Live Updates, allowing for more seamless and efficient updates. Additionally, Wear OS 7 will feature a visual refresh, including new Tile designs. Another key feature is the integration of Gemini, a new intelligence system. The update is expected to roll out in 2026, enhancing the overall user experience on Wear OS devices. Furthermore, Google is also updating its emoji on Android to 3D, which will bring a more physical and engaging experience to users, starting with Pixel phones later this year. These updates aim to improve the functionality and aesthetics of Google's wearable and mobile operating systems.

stories.headline: Google just ended the era of unlimited AI Google’s new Gemini usage limits are frustrating paying users in 2026. Here’s why AI subscriptions suddenly feel more expensive.
stories.summary: Google has introduced new usage limits for its Gemini AI model, ending the era of unlimited AI usage. The updated limits consider factors such as chat length, features used, and prompt complexity, with more powerful prompts counting towards the quota faster. This change has frustrated paying users, making AI subscriptions feel more expensive. The new limits apply to all users, including those on the Google AI Pro plan, which was recently downgraded. Gemini is Google's largest and most capable AI model, trained to be multimodal and recognize, understand, and generate human-like responses. The update has sparked complaints, with some users canceling their subscriptions due to the new restrictions. The change reflects a shift towards premium AI services, with Google tightening limits to manage usage and potentially increase revenue.

stories.headline: Petition asking Sony to develop Destiny 3 reaches 71K signatures Destiny 2 is going into maintenance mode, and fans want Destiny 3, so they've opened a petition asking Sony to greenlight and approve a new Destiny sequel.
stories.summary: A petition asking Sony to develop Destiny 3 has gained significant traction, with over 71,000 signatures. The petition was launched after Bungie announced that Destiny 2 would be entering maintenance mode, ending its live-service development. Fans are calling on Sony to greenlight and fund the development of a new Destiny sequel. The petition, started by a Destiny fan on Change.org, has quickly gained momentum. The move comes amid recent news about potential layoffs at Bungie and the end of Destiny 2's development cycle. With the community showing strong support for a new installment, the petition aims to persuade Sony to approve the development of Destiny 3. The number of signatures continues to grow, demonstrating the dedication and enthusiasm of the Destiny fan base.

stories.headline: HOVERAir AQUA Now in the Philippines The HOVERAir AQUA, the world's first fully waterproof self-flying camera, has been launched in the Philippines. The HOVERAir AQUA is designed for water-based ac
stories.summary: The HOVERAir AQUA, a fully waterproof self-flying camera, has been launched in the Philippines. Designed for water-based activities like kayaking, surfing, and jet skiing, it automatically tracks and records subjects without needing a remote pilot. Weighing under 250 grams, the drone has an IP67 rating, indicating its waterproof capability. The HOVERAir AQUA is priced at PHP 87,990 in the Philippines and was also launched on Indiegogo with early bird pricing starting at $999 USD. This innovative device is the world's first 100% waterproof aerial camera, making it ideal for capturing water adventures. The launch follows the success of HoverAir's previous product, the HoverAir X1, a palm-sized auto-flying camera drone known for its ease of use and social media-ready footage. The HOVERAir AQUA aims to provide a similar user experience for water-based activities.

stories.headline: Black Starlets miss out on FIFA U17 World Cup after suffering an 8-7 penalty shootout defeat to Uganda
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Starlets have missed out on the 2026 FIFA U17 World Cup after losing 8-7 in a penalty shootout to Uganda. The match had ended 2-2 after extra time, leading to the shootout. This defeat extends Ghana's absence from the tournament to nine years. The Black Starlets had a spirited campaign in Morocco but ultimately fell short. Head Coach Dr. Prosper Narteh Ogum and his team will now regroup and focus on the next qualification cycle. The loss means Ghana will not participate in the 2026 FIFA U17 World Cup, a significant setback for the team. The Black Starlets' impressive campaign was not enough to secure a spot in the global tournament. They will have to wait for the next opportunity to qualify.

stories.headline: Knicks near finals, take 3-0 lead vs Cavaliers
stories.summary: The New York Knicks have taken a 3-0 lead in the Eastern Conference Finals, defeating the Cleveland Cavaliers 121-108 in Game 3. The win brings the Knicks one step closer to their first NBA Finals appearance since 1999. The game, played in Cleveland, saw a balanced team effort from the Knicks, who dominated the Cavaliers to secure the victory. The series will continue with Game 4, scheduled to take place on Monday at 8:00pm ET on ESPN. The Cavaliers will look to mount a comeback, while the Knicks aim to advance to the NBA Finals with one more win. The Knicks' 3-0 lead puts significant pressure on the Cavaliers, who must win four consecutive games to overcome the deficit.

stories.headline: Auckland FC celebrates A-League championship with parade
stories.summary: Auckland FC celebrated their A-League Men championship title with a bus parade on Sunday. The team defeated Sydney FC 1-0 in the grand final on Saturday night at Go-Media Stadium in front of a record crowd of over 28,000 fans. This marks Auckland FC's first A-League Men championship title, achieved in just their second season. The parade took place along Queen Street, with thousands of supporters cheering on the players. A trophy presentation was held at Takutai Square in Britomart, allowing fans to celebrate with the team. The Mayor was among those in attendance at the stadium on Saturday, witnessing the Black Knights' historic 1-0 win over five-time A-League champions Sydney FC. The championship win is a significant achievement for the club and the city.

stories.headline: NBA Legend Magic Johnson Calls Out Cleveland Cavaliers
stories.summary: NBA legend Magic Johnson criticized the Cleveland Cavaliers' effort and body language after their 121-108 loss to the New York Knicks, which put them down 3-0 in the series. Johnson expressed disappointment in the team's performance, particularly at home. This follows a Game 1 loss where the Cavaliers blew a 22-point lead, with Charles Barkley calling it a "choke job." The Cavaliers' chances of turning the series around appear slim, with Johnson previously stating that their inability to recover from the Game 1 loss would be deflating. The Knicks' 3-0 lead has Johnson convinced that they can win a championship, even on nights when key players like Jalen Brunson don't have a big game. The Cavaliers' struggles have drawn criticism from multiple NBA legends, highlighting their struggles to overcome adversity.

stories.headline: Woman carries mother-in-law, 90, on back for 9 km to draw her pension from bank
stories.summary: A woman, Sukhmaniya Bai, carried her 90-year-old mother-in-law, Sonwari, 9 km on foot to a bank in rural Surguja, Chhattisgarh, for pension verification. The mandatory physical biometric verification at banks requires beneficiaries to be present in person, causing hardship for elderly citizens. Due to lack of transport and infrastructure, Sukhmaniya Bai had to walk the long distance with her mother-in-law on her back. The effort was successful, and the bank disbursed Sonwari's three months' pension, amounting to Rs 1,500. A video of the incident has gone viral, highlighting the difficulties faced by villagers in accessing basic services due to poor transport and infrastructure. The incident has triggered strong reactions online, drawing attention to the challenges faced by rural communities.

stories.headline: India issues advisory on Ebola outbreak, lists countries to avoid for travel
stories.summary: India has issued a travel advisory urging citizens to avoid non-essential travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan due to the Ebola outbreak. The advisory comes after the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the Ebola outbreak a public health emergency. The Indian government has assessed countries bordering the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, including South Sudan, to be at high risk of disease transmission. Citizens are advised to exercise caution and avoid traveling to these countries unless essential. The advisory is a precautionary measure to prevent the spread of the disease and protect Indian citizens from the growing Ebola outbreak in parts of Africa. The government will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as necessary.

stories.headline: Avoid non-essential travel: India's advisory for 3 African nations amid Ebola surge
stories.summary: India has advised citizens to avoid non-essential travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan due to the Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organisation (WHO) declared the outbreak a global health emergency, prompting the Indian government to issue a health advisory. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare warned citizens to strictly follow public health guidelines when traveling to or residing in these countries. Passengers arriving from or transiting through Ebola-affected countries are required to report to airport health authorities if they exhibit symptoms or have an exposure history. The advisory asks Indian nationals to avoid all non-essential travel to the affected countries until further notice, in line with WHO recommendations. The move aims to prevent the spread of the disease and protect Indian citizens.

stories.headline: Telangana heatwave death toll rises sharply as 51 die on Saturday alone
stories.summary: Telangana reported 51 heatstroke deaths on Saturday, bringing the overall death toll due to rising temperatures to over 100. The deaths occurred amid an intensifying heatwave, with temperatures remaining above 46 degrees Celsius in several districts. The Warangal district was the worst affected, reporting 23 deaths. This follows 34 heat-related deaths on Friday and 22 on Thursday. Most of the deceased were elderly and laborers. The heatwave has been relentless, with temperatures reaching a scorching 46 degrees Celsius on Saturday. The total death toll over three days exceeds 100, with Telangana being the most affected region, accounting for 30 of the 40 deaths reported on Saturday, according to local reports. The state government has yet to comment on the rising death toll and measures to mitigate the effects of the heatwave.

stories.headline: RBI's record dividend to US-Iran war: Top five triggers that may dictate the Indian stock market this week
stories.summary: The Indian stock market may be influenced by several key factors this week. The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) record dividend payout is expected to have a positive impact. However, escalating tensions between the US and Iran could lead to volatility. Crude oil prices will also be closely watched, as they can affect the Indian economy. Additionally, foreign institutional investor (FII) activity and the rupee's performance against the US dollar will be monitored. These factors may dictate the market's movement, following a strong weekly performance last week. The ongoing conflict between Israel and Iran is also a concern, with potential implications for Indian stocks. Overall, a combination of domestic and global factors will shape the Indian stock market's trajectory this week.

stories.headline: Indian stock market: On Friday, the Nifty 50 climbed 0.32% to end at 23,719.30, while the Sensex gained 0.23% to settle at 75,415.35
stories.summary: The Indian stock market ended the week with modest gains. The Nifty 50 climbed 0.32% to close at 23,719.30, while the Sensex gained 0.23% to settle at 75,415.35. Earlier in the day, the BSE Sensex had risen 491.02 points to reach 75,940.06, and the NSE Nifty had advanced 163.30 points to reclaim 23,070.90. The market breadth remained steady, with the advance-decline ratio indicating a positive tone. The Nifty 50 closed with a gain of 64.60 points, or 0.27%, at 23,719.30. The Sensex also ended with a gain, despite some selective gains across segments. The Indian markets ended the session on a broadly positive note.

stories.headline: US-Iran war concerns may impact Indian stock market
stories.summary: The Indian stock market may be impacted by concerns over a potential US-Iran war. The Sensex is closely watching the developments, with crude oil prices and Q4 results for FY26 being key triggers this week. US President Donald Trump stated that Chinese President Xi Jinping wants a deal made on Iran, according to a Bloomberg report. However, the White House believes Iran's latest proposal to end the war is insufficient for a deal. Oil prices have dropped and stock markets have risen after reports of a potential deal to end the Iran war. The situation remains volatile, with the Indian stock market likely to be influenced by further developments in the US-Iran conflict. Investors are advised to stay updated on the latest news and analysis from reputable sources.

stories.headline: RBI's dividend payout may boost Indian stock market sentiment
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is set to announce a record dividend payout to the government, estimated to be between Rs 2.7 lakh crore and Rs 3 lakh crore, surpassing last year's Rs 2.69 lakh crore payout. The RBI board will meet on May 22 to consider the surplus transfer for FY27. This payout is expected to provide a significant fiscal cushion to the government at the start of the new financial year. The record dividend is attributed to the central bank's strong performance and public sector banks posting historic profits in FY26. The announcement is likely to boost Indian stock market sentiment, offering a positive outlook for the economy. The exact amount of the dividend payout will be confirmed after the RBI board meeting.

stories.headline: South Korea to launch leveraged stock ETFs on Samsung, SK Hynix - Bloomberg Investing.com -- South Korea is set to launch its first single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds this week, offering investors products linked to semiconduc
stories.summary: South Korea is set to launch its first single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) tied to Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. The launch aims to attract retail trading activity back to domestic markets after investors turned to overseas markets. Analysts estimate net inflows into the 14 leveraged ETFs could reach 5.3 trillion won ($3.5 billion), with around 300,000 investors expected to participate. The ETFs will offer investors products linked to the semiconductor sector, allowing for leveraged exposure to the two chip giants. The move is part of South Korean regulators' efforts to boost domestic market activity and provide investors with new investment options. The launch is expected to take place this week, marking a significant development in the country's financial market.

stories.headline: The tokenized asset market topped $34 billion as U.S. Treasury products led a rapid expansion across blockchain-based finance. Market data showed the
stories.summary: The tokenized asset market has reached $34.01 billion, driven by the growth of U.S. Treasury products and increased institutional adoption of blockchain-based finance. Market data shows the sector has expanded more than tenfold since mid-2024. Tokenized U.S. Treasury products make up the largest share of the market. The rapid growth is attributed to the increasing use of blockchain technology in financial applications, with institutional players driving demand for complex financial products. The market's significant expansion, from under $1 billion to nearly $34 billion, has raised interest among retail investors about its potential for further growth. Distributed tokenized asset value is now at $34.01 billion, according to market data platform rwa.xyz, indicating a substantial increase in the adoption of tokenized assets.

stories.headline: GLOBALFOUNDRIES (GFS) is back in focus after launching Quantum Technology Solutions, a dedicated quantum manufacturing business supported by a planned US$375 mi
stories.summary: GlobalFoundries has launched Quantum Technology Solutions, a dedicated quantum manufacturing business. The new business aims to scale manufacturing capabilities for the quantum industry to achieve utility-scale quantum computing. It is supported by a planned $375 million commitment from the US Department of Commerce, which will also take a roughly 1% equity stake. The business is built on years of cryogenic innovation and partnerships with leading quantum innovators, driven by industry demand. Quantum Technology Solutions will support multiple qubit approaches, including superconducting, trapped ion, and photonic. The initiative aims to expand domestic quantum manufacturing capabilities, with the funding expected to facilitate the growth of the quantum industry. The launch of Quantum Technology Solutions marks a significant development in GlobalFoundries' efforts to support the advancement of quantum computing.

stories.headline: Freetrailer Group (DB:R0C) Margin Slip To 11% Tests Bullish Earnings Growth Narrative How Freetrailer Group’s Latest Numbers Set the Stage for the Story Freetrailer Group (DB:R0C) opened 2026 with Q1 revenue of 35.7 million DKK and net income of
stories.summary: Freetrailer Group (DB:R0C) reported Q1 2026 revenue of 35.7 million DKK and net income of 0.1 million DKK. The company's trailing twelve month figures show revenue of 159.9 million DKK and net income of 17.6 million DKK, with EPS of 2.10 DKK. In 2025, revenue was 144 million DKK and operating profit was 27 million DKK. Freetrailer Group expects to continue delivering strong double-digit growth in the underlying business, along with solid profits, despite increased investments in future growth and business models in 2026. The company's margin slipped to 11%, testing the bullish earnings growth narrative. Quarterly revenue has been increasing, moving from 28.3 million DKK in a recent period. The company's financials and stock performance are available for analysis, with key statistics including valuation measures and trading records.
